title: Rosalind and the Oath
premise: Juniper Vasquez, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Veth, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Lantern, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, Juniper discovers their own memories have been edited: they once carried a fragment of the god's dying voice, and someone paid the guild to erase it. Hunting the truth drags them into an alliance of found family—a disgraced wardwright, a starless oracle, and a rival ledger-keeper—while the old empire moves to reclaim the god's power and reignite the war it ended. In the end, Juniper must choose between restoring Veth (and the ancient war his return would spark) or speaking the god's true name aloud so he can finally die; they choose truth over loyalty, release the god, and rebuild the guild as keepers of memory rather than traders in it.
about_author: Kestrel Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal trading cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, oaths, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A quiet night at the Gilded Lantern: Juniper audits entries for bottled storms and borrowed years, establishing the guild's rules and their role as oath-bound record-keeper. A client pays an obscene sum to have 'one memory, name withheld' erased from the vault. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine—the erased entry is dated the day Juniper's own earliest memory begins.

chapters.title: What the God Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Flashback woven through present: the oath to Veth, taken as a starving child soldier, and the night ten years ago when the god's voice went silent mid-sentence. Juniper performs the daily rites anyway, alone. Emotional beat: stubborn devotion masking grief and abandonment.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The border wards fail in cascading rings; the sky goes starless from horizon to horizon. The guild master orders everyone inside and burns correspondence. Juniper notices the wards didn't break—they were switched off, from within, using a key only oath-bearers carry. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Wardwright Without Wards
chapters.summary: Sera Iln's POV. Sera, a disgraced imperial wardwright turned drunk, is dragged to the Lantern because her signature is on the fallen wards—forged, she swears. She and Juniper recognize each other from the war. She agrees to investigate for payment in 'one impossible thing.' Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's scars.

chapters.title: Entries Missing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Auditing the vault, Juniper finds gaps—pages excised cleanly, decades of transactions around one recurring client: the Chantry of the Silent Star. Worse, their own handwriting appears on pages describing events Juniper cannot remember living. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt; the horror of being an unreliable record of oneself.

chapters.title: The Oracle Who Sees Nothing
chapters.summary: Marrow's POV. Marrow, a young oracle whose gift died with the stars, begs sanctuary at the Lantern after their temple casts them out. Juniper takes them in against guild policy. Marrow's last vision, spoken in fever: 'The god is not silent. He is being eaten.' Emotional beat: found family beginning—an act of small defiance.

chapters.title: The Chantry of the Silent Star
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper infiltrates a Chantry service and finds priests worshipping the starless sky as holy silence—and its high priest wearing a guild signet ring that should be buried with the founder. Emotional beat: betrayal; the guild's hands are not clean, and neither, perhaps, are Juniper's.

chapters.title: Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera decodes the forged wards: they were keyed to an oath-bearer's blood—oath-bearers like Juniper. Confronting Juniper, she forces the question: what did you do ten years ago? Juniper cannot answer, and both know that's the answer. Emotional beat: alliance strained by accusation; loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: The Vault Below the Vault
chapters.summary: Juniper and Sera's alternating POV. Behind the ledger room, they find a hidden archive: records of the guild's founding purpose—not trade, but containment. The guild was built to imprison the last fragment of Veth's voice. And the current guild master has been selling pieces of it. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of everything Juniper served.

chapters.title: Guild Master's Terms
chapters.summary: Guild Master Corvane's POV. Corvane reveals he knows Juniper found the archive. He offers partnership: sell the god's voice to the resurgent empire, end the guild's poverty, spare Juniper's found family. He claims the stars went out because Veth is waking and must be kept sedated. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as protection.

chapters.title: What Marrow Remembers
chapters.summary: Marrow's POV. Marrow's visions return in fragments: they saw the erasure transaction ten years ago as a child—a mercenary selling the god's voice to save their company. The description matches Juniper. Marrow says nothing, torn between new family and terrible truth. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth embodied in the youngest character.

chapters.title: The Empire Sends Regards
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Imperial soldiers arrive demanding the guild honor an old contract: delivery of 'the asset.' Corvane stalls; a skirmish in the streets kills two guild members who took Juniper in years ago. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized—the cost of Juniper's secrets paid in other people's blood.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Cornered by Sera and Marrow, Juniper finally remembers: during the war's last battle, dying comrades begged Veth for mercy; the god poured his voice into Juniper to heal them, and Juniper—terrified of the burden—sold it to the guild to be contained. Emotional beat: shame, relief, and the first honest breath in ten years.

chapters.title: Ledger-Breakers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The trio resolves to steal the voice back before the empire collects. Sera can reopen the wards but needs an oath-bearer's willing blood freely given—which means Juniper must re-oath to a god they've resented for a decade. Emotional beat: forgiveness begins as a practical decision.

chapters.title: The Rite of Return
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The re-oathing ceremony in the ruined chapel: Juniper speaks the old vows not out of faith but choice, and feels Veth stir faintly inside the sealed fragment—enough to learn the god has been conscious, imprisoned, all along. Emotional beat: devotion transformed from obligation into responsibility.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane, revealed as the founder's descendant, believes containing the god saved the world once and will again; the empire's offer is leverage to keep the seal strong forever. He locks down the guild and brands Juniper, Sera, and Marrow as thieves in the ledgers—erasing them officially. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; conviction as dangerous as greed.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Marrow's POV. Using their returning sight, Marrow guides the trio through the vault's dream-locked lower levels while imperial forces breach above. Sera is gravely wounded holding a door. Emotional beat: fear and ferocity; the found family fights like it has something worth losing.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Dark
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Alone before the containment seal, Juniper speaks with Veth directly at last. The god does not demand freedom or worship—he asks to be allowed to die, as gods do when their war is truly over, and warns that his resurrection by the empire would reignite the ancient war. Emotional beat: awe, tenderness, and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Everything Owed
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The empire seizes the guild; Corvane, desperate, attempts to transfer the voice into himself rather than surrender it. Sera collapses the wards around the vault; Marrow holds the collapsing visions open long enough for Juniper to reach the seal. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, every debt called due at once.

chapters.title: The True Name
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Climax. To free Veth into death, Juniper must speak the god's true name—the secret the whole story has been about—but speaking it aloud means any empire agent could later use it. Juniper speaks it anyway, then writes it in the ledger and burns the page, making themselves its only keeper. Veth dies gently; the stars relight. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Entered in Full
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The empire retreats leaderless; Corvane, broken by the god's death, surrenders the guild. Sera survives her wounds; Marrow's sight settles into something bearable. Juniper is voted the new guild master and refuses—then accepts on condition the guild stop trading in impossible things and start safeguarding them. Emotional beat: exhausted peace, tentative hope.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Oath
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Epilogue. Juniper opens a fresh ledger and writes the guild's new first entry: the full account of Veth's life and death, including their own crime and confession, signed with the name 'Rosalind'—the name Veth gave them as a child, which they sold away and have now reclaimed. Emotional beat: wholeness; memory kept honestly at last.
